You are auditing a draft answer to a visual set reporting task. Task: Find every individual product on the shelves in the image: each separately visible package or item, including partly visible ones.

The next image is the scene; the image after it is the same scene with the draft objects drawn as numbered red marks. The draft is a hypothesis: it may contain wrong, duplicated or badly placed objects and it may miss objects. Do two things: (1) check the existing draft objects against the image; (2) scan the whole image for target objects missing from the draft, including areas with no red mark. No mark in a region is not evidence that the region is empty.

Each object is given by x1, y1, x2, y2, the edges of its axis-aligned bounding box normalized to the FULL IMAGE (0 <= x1 < x2 <= 1, 0 <= y1 < y2 <= 1, four decimals). Draft objects in the text payload are normalized to the full image.

Return only atomic edits: "add" ("new": a list of one or more objects), "delete" ("ids": draft objects that are not real target objects, are duplicates, or do not exist), "replace" (one id, one new object: corrects the position or label of the same object), "split" (one id, two or more new objects), "merge" (two or more ids, one new object). Every edit has "evidence": at most twelve words about what is visible. Do not delete a real object whose position is only inaccurate; use replace. Overlap alone does not prove a duplicate. At most 32 edits, most important first. If the draft needs no change, return {"edits": []}.

Output contract: one JSON object {"edits": [...]}. No prose, no code fence.

The first image is the reference crop of one target instance. The next four images are overlapping crops of the scene at native resolution: crop 1 top-left, crop 2 top-right, crop 3 bottom-left, crop 4 bottom-right, with the draft objects drawn as numbered red marks. The draft is a hypothesis: it may contain wrong, duplicated or badly placed objects and it may miss objects. Do two things: (1) check the existing draft objects against the image; (2) scan the whole image for target objects missing from the draft, including areas with no red mark. No mark in a region is not evidence that the region is empty.

New objects have "crop" (1 to 4) and coordinates normalized to THAT CROP. Each object is given by x and y, the coordinates of its center normalized to the crop (0 <= x < 1, 0 <= y < 1, four decimals). Draft objects in the text payload are normalized to the full image.

Return only atomic edits: "add" ("new": a list of one or more objects), "delete" ("ids": draft objects that are not real target objects, are duplicates, or do not exist), "replace" (one id, one new object: corrects the position or label of the same object), "split" (one id, two or more new objects), "merge" (two or more ids, one new object). Every edit has "evidence": at most twelve words about what is visible. Do not delete a real object whose position is only inaccurate; use replace. Overlap alone does not prove a duplicate. At most 32 edits, most important first. If the draft needs no change, return {"edits": []}.

Output contract: one JSON object {"edits": [...]}. No prose, no code fence.
